driver: R27A09-GAL4, nSyb-GAL80, UAS-flp, nSyb-LexA, LexAop>STOP>TRPA1 (Supplementary file 1, Behav); Video 17 legend: TRPA1 under control of R27A09
preparation_detail: decapitated adult females on a hot plate (Materials and methods)
effector: TRPA1 (dTRPA1; LexAop>STOP>TRPA1), heat ramp 24 to 37 C
coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1 off-target expression for the 18B line: 'Abdominal motorneurons'. Text: 'Lineage 18 is missing from T1 and only the 18B hemilineage persists in T2 and T3'. Discussion: 'In all cases, the predominant expression in the line was from the target hemilineage.' The source does not say the driver misses part of 18B.
locator: Results, 'Hemilineage 18B', PDF pp. 18-19; Figure 7E legend (p. 20); Video 17 legend (p. 21); Figure 9A row 18B (p. 26); Supplementary file 1 row 18B
quote: the fly would jump and the wing movements would transition into flapping, but not consistently in that order
other_observation: Text also: 'the decapitated flies typically initiated walking and that was sometimes accompanied by jerky wing movements with the wings remaining partially folded.' Fig 7E (high-speed): 'Flapping often began prior to wing raising causing the wings to bend'. Figure 9A: 18B has large walking (marked * = progression of behaviours during the ramp), wing buzz and takeoff bars plus a small wing-wave bar; no bars in the change-in-posture or uncoordinated-leg columns. Video 17 montage (side view, 24 frames over 5.2 s) shows a decapitated fly with moving wings that then becomes airborne.
notes: d2-d4 unclear: walking and the jump are reported without saying which legs (Results general text says high-speed video confirmed 'the role of the t2 legs in producing the takeoff jump' in lines where takeoff was common, but this is not stated for 18B specifically, so d3 is not coded yes). d5/d6/d7 'no' from Figure 9A, where the 18B row shows no bar for change in posture or uncoordinated leg movements. d12 unclear: wing raising occurs within the takeoff sequence (Fig 7E) but is not described as held; during walking the wings stay 'partially folded'. Penetrance: Figure 9A gives bars on a 0-100% scale (15-25 flies per group) but exact values cannot be read reliably from the image; no number is given in the text.

driver: R32E04-GAL4, UAS-TRPA1 (Supplementary file 1, Behav); Video 18 legend: TRPA1 under control of R32E04
preparation_detail: decapitated adult females on a hot plate (Materials and methods)
coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1 off-target expression for the 19A line: '1-2 neurons per thoracic neuromere; ~ 10-20 neurons in abdomen'. Discussion: 'In all cases, the predominant expression in the line was from the target hemilineage.' The source does not say the driver misses part of 19A.
locator: Results, 'Hemilineages 19A and 19B', PDF p. 19; Figure 7I legend (p. 20); Video 18 legend (p. 21); Figure 9A row 19A (p. 26); Supplementary file 1 row 19A
quote: the decapitated flies stayed in place and showed no movements of their T1 or T3 legs, but their T2 legs show incessant waving movements
other_observation: Figure 7I legend: 'With increased temperature the flies extend their T2 legs and begin to wave them. The frames for a one second period (18-19 s) are superimposed to illustrate movements of the T2 legs (arrow) and stability of the others.' Waving 'continue[s] for the duration of the thermal activation'. Figure 9A: large uncoordinated-leg-movement bar, a small change-in-posture bar, and no bars for walking, wing wave, wing buzz or takeoff. Video 18 montage (top view, 24 frames over 39 s) shows flies staying in place.
notes: d7 yes: repeated T2 leg waving, which the source does not call walking and which Figure 9A scores as uncoordinated leg movement. d8 'no': 'stayed in place' and no walking bar in Figure 9A. d5/d6 unclear: Figure 7I says the flies 'extend their T2 legs' and then wave them (not described as a held extension), and Figure 9A shows a small change-in-posture bar without saying flexion or extension. d10-d13 'no' because the Figure 9A row has no bars for wing wave, wing buzz or takeoff. Penetrance: bar values in Figure 9A cannot be read reliably; none is given in the text.

driver: R24G06-LexA, LexAop-TRPA1 (Supplementary file 1, Behav); Video 19 legend: TRPA1 under control of R24G06
preparation_detail: decapitated adult females on a hot plate (Materials and methods)
coverage_notes: The source treats 20A and 22A as one unit: 'We were unable to recover lines that distinguished them, and have treated them as a single entity in the adult.' Supplementary file 1 off-target expression for the 20A,22A line: 'none'.
locator: Results, 'Hemilineages 20A and 22A', PDF p. 19; Figure 7N legend (p. 20); Video 19 legend (p. 22); Figure 9A row '20A, 22A' (p. 26); Supplementary file 1 row 20A,22A
quote: As the temperature increased, the flies extended their legs until they had assumed a splayed out posture
other_observation: Text: 'Activation of the 20A/22A interneurons evoked a simple change in posture' and 'Occasional grooming bouts occurred during and after the change in posture.' Figure 7N legend: 'they splay out their legs as the temperature rises.' Figure 9A: large change-in-posture bar; no uncoordinated-leg or takeoff bar; what appear to be very small bars in the walking and wing-buzz columns. Video 19 montage (top view, 24 frames over 49.6 s) shows the legs becoming progressively splayed.
notes: 'Their legs' is read as all legs (d2-d4 yes, per protocol convention). d6 yes: a sustained leg extension into a splayed posture. d5 'no': the source describes the posture change only as extension. d9 yes: grooming bouts during activation (the text says 'during and after'). d8/d11/d12/d13 unclear: Figure 9A seems to show very small walking and wing-buzz bars for this row, but they cannot be read with confidence at the available resolution and the text mentions no walking or wing movement. d7 and d10 'no' because Figure 9A shows no bar in those columns. One record covers both 20A and 22A because the source could not separate them.

driver: R26H05-GAL4AD, R51H05-GAL4DBD, UAS-flp, LexAop>STOP>TRPA1, nSyb-LexA (Supplementary file 1, Behav); text: 'the R51H05-GAL4 line'; Video 20 legend: TRPA1 under control of R51H05
preparation_detail: decapitated adult females on a hot plate (Materials and methods)
effector: TRPA1 (dTRPA1; LexAop>STOP>TRPA1), heat ramp 24 to 32 C
coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1 off-target expression for the 21A line: '3-5 neurons/ thoracic segment; abdominal motoneurons'. Discussion: 'In all cases, the predominant expression in the line was from the target hemilineage.' The source does not say the driver misses part of 21A.
locator: Results, 'Hemilineage 21A', PDF p. 21; Figure 7Q legend (p. 20); Video 20 legend (p. 22); Figure 9A row 21A (p. 26); Supplementary file 1 row 21A
quote: uncoordinated leg movements that lacked both intralimb and interlimb coordination. The leg movements were incessant during the stimulation
other_observation: Text: 'typically, the flies did not move from their place'. Figure 7Q legend: 'Eventually the flies become immobile with their legs frozen at unusual angles (21 s). The frames for an intermediate, one second period (10-11 s) are superimposed to show the transient hyperkinetic leg movements.' Figure 9A: large uncoordinated-leg bar, a small change-in-posture bar, no walking or takeoff bar, and what appear to be very small wing-wave and wing-buzz bars. Video 20 montage (top view, 24 frames over 43 s) shows clustered flies with legs in varied positions.
notes: d2-d4 yes: the Figure 7Q legend refers to 'their legs' (all legs) frozen at unusual angles, and the text refers to interlimb movements. d5/d6 unclear: the legs are held 'frozen at unusual angles', not described as flexion or extension. The text calls the leg movements 'incessant during the stimulation', while the Figure 7Q legend says the flies 'eventually' become immobile; both are recorded. d8 'no': the flies did not move from their place and Figure 9A has no walking bar. d11-d13 unclear: possible very small wing bars in Figure 9A that cannot be read with confidence; the text mentions no wing movement. d10 'no' because there is no takeoff bar in Figure 9A.

driver: R77C10-GAL4, UAS_TRPA1 (Supplementary file 1, Behav); text: 'line R77C10-GAL4'; Video 21 legend: TRPA1 under control of R77C10
preparation_detail: decapitated adult females on a hot plate (Materials and methods)
effector: UAS-TRPA1 (dTRPA1), heat ramp 24 to 32 C (Video 21 legend); the Figure 7T frame is labelled 36 C
coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1 off-target expression for the 23B line: 'none'.
locator: Results, 'Hemilineage 23B', PDF pp. 21-22; Figure 7T legend (pp. 20-21); Video 21 legend (p. 22); Figure 9A row 23B (p. 26); Supplementary file 1 row 23B
quote: caused a progressive higher frequency of intersegmental limb movements but the intralimb coordination of limb joints appeared to be quite poor
other_observation: Figure 7T legend: 'Stimulation of the 23B neurons produce uncoordinated leg movements and the flies basically stay in place (36 C).' Figure 9A: large change-in-posture and uncoordinated-leg bars, no takeoff bar, and what appear to be very small walking and wing-buzz bars. Video 21 montage (top view, 24 frames): in the later frames several flies change position and orientation and some leave the field of view. This was not used as evidence of walking because the source does not describe it as walking.
notes: d2-d4 unclear: 'limb movements' / 'leg movements' without saying which legs. d7 yes: repeated, uncoordinated leg movements. d5/d6 unclear: Figure 9A shows a large change-in-posture bar, but no source text says whether this is flexion or extension. d8 unclear: the flies 'basically stay in place', but Figure 9A may show a very small walking bar. d11-d13 unclear: possible very small wing-buzz bar in Figure 9A; the text mentions no wing movement. d10 'no' because there is no takeoff bar in Figure 9A. The heat-ramp range differs between the Video 21 legend (24 to 32 C) and the Figure 7T panel label (36 C); both are recorded.

driver: R15A03-GAL4 (text); Supplementary file 1 Behav row: 'R15A03-GAL4, nSyb-GAL80, UAS-flp, nSyb-LexA, LexAop>STOP>GFP'; Video 22 legend says 'under control of R22G11'
preparation_detail: decapitated adult females on a hot plate (Materials and methods)
effector: TRPA1 (dTRPA1) per the Video 22 legend, heat ramp 24 to 32 C
coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1 off-target expression for the 24B line: 'Occasional descending axons; <10 abdominal neurons'. The source does not say the driver misses part of 24B. 24B is a motor hemilineage: 'all of the B daughters are leg motoneurons'.
locator: Results, 'Hemilineage 24B', PDF p. 22; Figure 7W legend (p. 21); Video 22 legend (p. 23); Supplementary file 1 row 24B
quote: Stimulation of the 24B motoneurons produced repetitive movements of the legs although these typically resulted in no net movement of the fly
other_observation: Text: 'By the end of the ramp the legs were often held at awkward angles. Rare wing movements occurred but these were usually associated with grooming attempts.' Figure 7W legend: 'At elevated temperatures the flies typically showed repetitive leg movements.' 24B does not appear in Figure 9A. Video 22 montage (top view, 24 frames over 42.9 s) shows flies mostly in place.
notes: 'Movements of the legs' is read as all legs (d2-d4 yes, per protocol convention). d7 yes: repetitive leg movements that are not described as walking. d8 'no': 'no net movement of the fly'. d5/d6 unclear: the legs are 'held at awkward angles', which is not described as flexion or extension. d9 yes: 'grooming attempts'. d11 yes: rare wing movements, mostly with grooming. d10/d12/d13 not_assessed: 24B is absent from Figure 9A and the text says nothing about takeoff or wing posture. Source inconsistencies, all recorded: the Video 22 legend names R22G11 (the 1A driver) while the text names R15A03; the Supplementary file 1 'Behav' genotype lists LexAop>STOP>GFP rather than TRPA1; and the section opens with 'Hemilineage 24A ... in which all of the B daughters are leg motoneurons' while the Figure 7 legend says 'Hemilineage 24'. Because the line has occasional descending axons, the Discussion says such lines were handled by ageing flies 24 h after decapitation or by tsh-GAL80, but which was done for 24B is not stated.
